quizName: DMV Practice Test #4 30 Questions • Passing Score 25

questions.question: Why is it important to keep space between your motorcycle and other vehicles?

options.text: It gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake.
It keeps you in one area of the lane and limits your movement.
It lets you depend on others to spot hazards.
It requires you to drive faster to keep up with traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: It gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake.
questions.explanation: Keeping space around your motorcycle gives you time and room to react if another driver makes a mistake.

questions.question: How does riding with a passenger affect your motorcycle?

options.text: It usually makes no difference in how the motorcycle handles.
It is usually safe for riders who are just starting out.
It can change how the motorcycle handles.
It is encouraged to help new riders get used to different situations.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can change how the motorcycle handles.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds extra weight, which changes how your motorcycle handles. Only experienced riders should carry passengers.

questions.question: What fabric gives motorcycle riders the best protection?

options.text: Leather
Denim
Wool
Polyester

questions.correctAnswerText: Leather
questions.explanation: Leather jackets and pants offer the most protection for motorcycle riders.

questions.question: What do goggles protect when you are riding?

options.text: Your eyes, but not the rest of your face.
Your face, but not your eyes.
Your eyes less well than eyeglasses.
Nothing at all.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your eyes, but not the rest of your face.
questions.explanation: Goggles protect your eyes. Only a face shield protects your entire face. Eyeglasses are not a good substitute for goggles or a face shield.

questions.question: Which of these is NOT important when choosing a motorcycle helmet?

options.text: The helmet meets U.S. Department of Transportation standards.
The helmet fits snugly all the way around your head.
The helmet has no cracks or loose padding.
The helmet looks cool.

questions.correctAnswerText: The helmet looks cool.
questions.explanation: A good helmet must meet U.S. Department of Transportation and state standards, fit snugly all around your head, and have no cracks, loose padding, or frayed straps. How it looks is not important for safety.

questions.question: What must you have to carry a passenger on your motorcycle?

options.text: A seat that is large enough for two riders.
Only one set of footrests.
A passenger who does not wear protective clothing.
A sticker on the brake light to warn other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: A seat that is large enough for two riders.
questions.explanation: Your motorcycle must have a seat large enough for two riders and footrests for the passenger. Your passenger should wear the same protective gear that riders wear.

questions.question: What should you do while riding your motorcycle?

options.text: Always look ahead and predict possible hazards.
Focus on the controls and speedometer instead of the road.
Do not worry about hazards because there are very few on the road.
Look ahead but do not look for hazards.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always look ahead and predict possible hazards.
questions.explanation: Always look well ahead to spot possible hazards. This helps you react to problems before they happen.

questions.question: Who is most likely to crash a motorcycle?

options.text: Experienced riders.
Beginning riders.
Those who know their motorcycle well.
Those who have taken a safety course.

questions.correctAnswerText: Beginning riders.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen most often with untrained, beginning riders who do not yet know their motorcycle.

questions.question: What should you do if a driver is following you too closely?

options.text: Do not worry about it.
Change lanes safely and let them pass.
Speed up.
Leave the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes safely and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is to let them pass you. Change lanes safely and let them go ahead. Speeding up may just make them tailgate you faster.

questions.question: If you wait one hour for each drink of alcohol before riding, what happens?

options.text: You cannot be arrested for drinking and riding.
Your riding skills will not be affected.
Alcohol effects may still remain in your system.
You will be safe as long as you ride slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Alcohol effects may still remain in your system.
questions.explanation: Your body processes about one drink per hour. However, alcohol can still build up in your system even at this rate. This buildup can still affect your ability to ride safely.

questions.question: How can you be more visible at an intersection?

options.text: Use your headlight while riding.
Swerve within your lane to get attention.
Raise your arms.
Avoid using your brakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your headlight while riding.
questions.explanation: Use your headlight and position your motorcycle in the lane where oncoming traffic can see you best. Keep space around your motorcycle so you can avoid danger if needed.

questions.question: More than half of all motorcycle crashes involve:

options.text: Speeds greater than 35 mph.
Riding at night.
Worn tires.
Riders with less than five months of experience on their motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riders with less than five months of experience on their motorcycle.
questions.explanation: More than half of motorcycle crashes involve riders with less than five months of experience on their motorcycle. If you are new to riding, practice in a safe, controlled area before riding on the road.

questions.question: Your lane position should:

options.text: Hide your plans from other drivers.
Invite other drivers to share your lane.
Help you see others and be seen.
Keep you close to road signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: Help you see others and be seen.
questions.explanation: Good lane position helps you see other road users and makes you more visible. It also helps you avoid wind blasts, blind spots, and road hazards. Your position should discourage others from sharing your lane and give you an escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: You can improve how visible you are by:

options.text: Adding extra lights to your motorcycle.
Not using your turn signal.
Wearing dark clothing.
Waving at people.

questions.correctAnswerText: Adding extra lights to your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Wear bright or reflective clothing to be more visible. Add extra lights to your motorcycle, use your turn signals, and flash your brake light when needed. These steps help other drivers notice you.

questions.question: Riding next to a car:

options.text: Is a good idea.
Can hide you in the driver's blind spot.
Is only a problem on wet roads.
Makes driving easier for the other driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can hide you in the driver's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding directly beside another vehicle is dangerous. You may be in the driver's blind spot where they cannot see you. The vehicle also blocks your escape path.

questions.question: A three-wheeled motorcycle:

options.text: Turns like a two-wheeled motorcycle.
Turns differently than a two-wheeled motorcycle.
Should not be used on curves.
Should use the shoulder when turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turns differently than a two-wheeled motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Three-wheeled motorcycles and motorcycles with sidecars turn differently than two-wheeled motorcycles.

questions.question: Riding gloves should:

options.text: Not be worn because they make your hands too hot.
Be worn to grip the handlebars better.
Not be worn because they make the controls hard to use.
Be worn only on cold days.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be worn to grip the handlebars better.
questions.explanation: Wear leather gloves or gloves made of another tough material. They give you a better grip on the handlebars and protect your hands if you crash.

questions.question: When riding on a slippery surface, you should:

options.text: Ride faster than normal.
Use only the front brake.
Slow down.
Use only the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Slow down when riding on slippery surfaces. Use both brakes when you brake and avoid sudden movements.

questions.question: Mirror checks:

options.text: Should be part of how you scan the road.
Should be avoided because they distract you.
Are not needed because other drivers see you easily.
Are only needed in bad weather.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be part of how you scan the road.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors often so you know what is behind you. Regular mirror checks should be part of your normal scanning routine for safety.

questions.question: After a motorcycle helmet is involved in a crash, it should be:

options.text: Inspected carefully.
Replaced.
Sold to another rider.
Given a new chinstrap.

questions.correctAnswerText: Replaced.
questions.explanation: Replace any helmet that has been worn during a crash.

questions.question: Can clothing help prevent injuries in a crash?

options.text: No, clothing does not protect you.
No, clothing is just a personal choice.
Yes, but only if clothing is very loose and flaps in the wind.
Yes, if a jacket and pants cover your arms and legs completely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, if a jacket and pants cover your arms and legs completely.
questions.explanation: Good clothing can reduce injury in a crash. Wear a jacket and pants made of sturdy material that cover your arms and legs. They should fit snug so they do not flap in the wind.

questions.question: You should do a complete check of your motorcycle:

options.text: Before every ride.
Once a week.
Once a month.
Once a year.

questions.correctAnswerText: Before every ride.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles need more frequent checks than cars. Check your motorcycle completely before every ride.

questions.question: Your body gets rid of almost ______ of alcohol per hour.

options.text: one drink
two drinks
three drinks
four drinks

questions.correctAnswerText: one drink
questions.explanation: On average, your body can eliminate the alcohol in about one drink per hour.

questions.question: A way to lower your risk of a crash is to:

options.text: Tell other drivers what you plan to do.
Not look ahead while riding.
Wear dark clothes.
Ride in parts of your lane that are hard to see.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell other drivers what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, make sure other drivers can see you. Use your signals and brake light. Position your motorcycle so it is visible. Keep space around your motorcycle and watch the road ahead, behind, and to the side.

questions.question: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield:

options.text: Is not needed if you have a windshield.
Only protects your eyes.
Protects your whole face.
Does not protect your face as well as goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protects your whole face.
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face in a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield is not enough protection by itself.

questions.question: For motorcycle safety, you should:

options.text: Trust that everything on your motorcycle will work.
Check your motorcycle before every ride.
Check your motorcycle once a month.
Check your motorcycle twice a week.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your motorcycle before every ride.
questions.explanation: A small problem on a motorcycle is more serious than on a car. Check your motorcycle thoroughly before every ride.

questions.question: Gloves can:

options.text: Make it hard to control your motorcycle and should be avoided.
Help other drivers see you.
Give you a better grip on the handlebars.
Offer no protection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give you a better grip on the handlebars.
questions.explanation: Gloves give you a better grip on your handlebars. They also protect your hands in a crash.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?

options.text: Warning
Service
Regulatory
Speed limit

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They tell drivers about upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: A leather jacket:

options.text: Can make a rider look cool.
Is usually too warm to wear when riding.
Protects you in a crash.
Should not be worn when riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Protects you in a crash.
questions.explanation: Wear a long-sleeved jacket, preferably leather, when riding to protect yourself. In warm weather, a leather jacket can help prevent dehydration. Many motorcycle jackets are designed to keep you cool in hot weather.

questions.question: To control your motorcycle well, you should:

options.text: Sit with your arms holding you up instead of steering.
Keep your knees against the gas tank for balance.
Let your feet hang off the footrests.
Sit so far back that you must stretch to reach the handgrips.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your knees against the gas tank for balance.
questions.explanation: Keep your knees against the gas tank to stay balanced in turns. Sit forward enough that your arms can steer without holding you up. Sit close enough that your arms are slightly bent when holding the handgrips. Keep your feet firmly on the footrests.
